beats.title: Madagascar's Elephant Birds Vanish
beats.description: The largest birds ever to live, towering flightless giants of an Indian Ocean island, disappeared after people settled there.
beats.note: Approximate; extinction estimates range roughly 1000-1200 CE, c. 1000 used. Not searched individually.

beats.title: New Zealand's Last Moa Disappear
beats.description: Hunting by the first Polynesian settlers wiped out all nine species of towering flightless birds within about a century.
beats.note: Approximate; a widely cited estimate of c. 1445. Not searched individually.

beats.title: The Last Aurochs Dies
beats.description: The final wild ox, ancestor of domestic cattle, died in a Polish forest after centuries of hunting and lost grazing land.
beats.why_in: last named survivor of a species

beats.title: The Dodo Is Last Seen
beats.description: The flightless bird of Mauritius, found by sailors less than a century earlier, was last reliably sighted on a small islet.
beats.note: Last widely accepted sighting is c. 1662.

beats.title: Steller's Sea Cow Is Hunted Out
beats.description: A giant, gentle relative of the manatee was wiped out in the Bering Sea within decades of its discovery by Europeans.

beats.title: The Bluebuck Disappears
beats.description: An antelope of South Africa's southern cape became the first large African mammal to be driven extinct in historic times.

beats.title: The Last Great Auks Are Killed
beats.description: Fishermen strangled the last known pair of the North Atlantic's flightless penguin-like seabird on a rocky Icelandic islet.

beats.title: Last Cape Lion Shot
beats.description: The large black-maned lion of South Africa's southern tip was shot out by hunters and settlers, ending a distinct subspecies.
beats.note: Last known wild one killed c. 1858.

beats.title: Tasmanian Emu Hunted to Extinction
beats.description: A dwarf emu of an island south of Australia was shot out by settlers and its last birds vanished from the wild.

beats.title: The Falkland Islands Wolf Is Killed
beats.description: The only native land mammal of its remote South Atlantic archipelago was hunted and poisoned out by settlers and sheep farmers.

beats.title: Last Labrador Duck Shot
beats.description: A shy sea duck of the North American Atlantic coast vanished with almost no record of why, the first endemic bird lost there.

beats.title: The Last Quagga Dies in Amsterdam
beats.description: A zebra relative with stripes only on its front half died alone in a European zoo, its wild kin shot out years earlier.

beats.title: The Sea Mink Is Gone
beats.description: The largest mink, prized for its fur on the North Atlantic coast, was trapped to extinction before scientists studied it properly.

beats.title: Stephens Island Wren Wiped Out
beats.description: A tiny flightless songbird of a small New Zealand island was destroyed soon after a lighthouse keeper's cat arrived.

beats.title: The Rocky Mountain Locust Vanishes
beats.description: Swarms once the size of a large state had darkened the American plains, yet the insect was gone after one last live specimen.

beats.title: The Japanese Wolf's Last Specimen
beats.description: A young wolf killed near a mountain town became the final record of Japan's small native wolf after rabies and persecution.

beats.title: The Huia Is Last Seen
beats.description: A prized New Zealand songbird, whose tail feathers were worn as ornaments and whose forest was cleared, was last seen alive.

beats.title: Martha, Last Passenger Pigeon, Dies
beats.description: The last of a species that once darkened American skies with billions of birds died alone in a Cincinnati zoo.

beats.title: Last Carolina Parakeet Dies
beats.description: The only parrot native to the eastern United States ended its story when its last captive, Incas, died in the same zoo as Martha.

beats.title: Last Wild Barbary Lion Shot
beats.description: The big, dark-maned lion of North Africa, a favourite of the Roman arena, was last shot in the wild in the Atlas Mountains.
beats.note: Last known wild lion shot c. 1922.

beats.title: Booming Ben, the Last Heath Hen
beats.description: The final eastern prairie chicken, a lone male nicknamed for his call, was last seen on an island off Massachusetts.

beats.title: Benjamin, the Last Thylacine, Dies
beats.description: The last known striped Tasmanian marsupial wolf died in a Hobart zoo, unprotected only weeks after its species gained legal cover.

beats.title: The Xerces Blue Butterfly Is Lost
beats.description: A small blue butterfly of the San Francisco peninsula became the first American insect known to vanish through urban development.

beats.title: Caribbean Monk Seal Last Sighted
beats.description: The only seal native to the warm Caribbean waters was last seen on a remote bank, after centuries of hunting for oil.

beats.title: The Caspian Tiger Fades Away
beats.description: A long-legged tiger of the lands around an inland sea was last seen, victim of hunting and the loss of its river forests.

beats.title: The Javan Tiger Is Last Recorded
beats.description: A small island tiger, once found across its Indonesian homeland, slipped away as forests were turned into farmland.

beats.title: Last Dusky Seaside Sparrow Dies
beats.description: The final bird of a marsh sparrow found only on one Florida coast died in captivity, a lone male named Orange Band.

beats.title: The Golden Toad Is Last Seen
beats.description: A brilliant orange amphibian from one Costa Rican cloud forest vanished, a warning sign of climate change and disease.

beats.title: Celia, Last Pyrenean Ibex, Dies
beats.description: The last wild wild-goat of her mountain range was found crushed by a fallen tree, later briefly cloned, then lost again.

beats.title: The Po'ouli Is Last Seen
beats.description: A rare, drab-looking Hawaiian forest bird, discovered only a few decades earlier, was last seen after a rescue attempt failed.

beats.title: Baiji Declared Functionally Extinct
beats.description: A survey of the Yangtze failed to find a single freshwater dolphin, the first dolphin lost to human activity.
beats.note: Survey end 2006 declared it functionally extinct.

beats.title: Lonesome George Dies
beats.description: The last Pinta Island giant tortoise, long the world's rarest creature, died in the Galapagos after decades without a mate.

beats.title: Sudan, Last Male White Rhino, Dies
beats.description: The final male of a northern subspecies, guarded around the clock by armed rangers in Kenya, was put down, leaving two females.

beats.title: Ivory-Billed Woodpecker Delisted
beats.description: A wildlife agency proposed removing a giant swamp woodpecker, long searched for, from the list of living birds.
beats.note: Proposal announced Sept 2021; final delisting later.

beats.title: Chinese Paddlefish Declared Extinct
beats.description: One of the largest freshwater fish on Earth, a Yangtze giant dating from the dinosaur age, was officially declared lost.
